questions.question: In out-of-order superscalar processor microarchitectures, why is register renaming fundamentally employed prior to instruction dispatch into reservation stations or issue queues?
options: To eliminate false data dependencies (Write-After-Read and Write-After-Write hazards) arising from a limited architectural register namespace.
To resolve true data dependencies (Read-After-Write hazards) by bypassing execution results directly around the physical register file.
To convert speculative branch instructions into unconditional jumps, minimizing branch misprediction penalties.
To compress 64-bit wide instructions into compact 32-bit representations inside the decoded instruction cache.
To ensure that load and store operations access the Level-1 data cache strictly in their original program order.

questions.question: In synchronous finite state machine (FSM) digital logic design, what is the fundamental structural distinction between a Moore machine and a Mealy machine?
options: A Moore machine updates its state on the active clock edge, whereas a Mealy machine updates state asynchronously without a clock.
A Moore machine's outputs depend solely on its current state, whereas a Mealy machine's outputs depend on both its current state and current primary inputs.
A Moore machine requires fewer flip-flops than an equivalent Mealy machine for any given regular language.
A Mealy machine contains purely combinational feedback loops without state registers, whereas a Moore machine strictly requires flip-flops.
A Mealy machine evaluates next-state logic using multiplexers, whereas a Moore machine strictly relies on ROM-based lookup tables.

questions.question: In shared-memory multiprocessor architectures, what is the root cause of the performance degradation phenomenon known as 'false sharing'?
options: Multiple threads access the same virtual address simultaneously, triggering redundant page faults in the memory management unit.
A processor core reads stale data from main memory because its local store buffer failed to flush before an external read request.
Independent threads on different cores update distinct, non-overlapping variables that reside within the same cache line, triggering continuous coherence invalidations.
Multiple cores issue concurrent write requests to identical memory locations, producing a protocol deadlock across the system crossbar.
An out-of-order execution engine speculates incorrectly on memory dependencies, causing repeated pipeline flushes across cores.

questions.question: In deep-submicron CMOS reliability analysis, what is the primary physical cause and operational impact of Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI)?
options: High current density in power rails displacing metal atoms into voids and hillocks over extended operating lifespans.
Hot electrons injecting into the thin gate oxide of NMOS devices during high-frequency switching, triggering punch-through breakdown.
Reverse-bias leakage current causing thermal runaway in the bulk substrate during deep standby sleep modes.

Generation of interface traps and oxide charges in PMOS transistors subjected to negative gate-to-source bias at elevated temperatures, increasing the absolute threshold voltage and degrading circuit path delays over time.
Spontaneous dielectric breakdown caused by plasma charge accumulation during reactive-ion etching of backend metallization layers.

questions.question: In standard-cell ASIC implementation and low-power digital design, what is the primary operational strategy of Multi-Threshold CMOS (Multi-Vt) optimization?
options: Applying dynamic forward body biasing to all standard cells across active clock cycles to reduce dynamic switching capacitance.
Fabricating all sequential elements with Low-Vt transistors and all combinational logic with Ultra-High-Vt transistors regardless of timing slack.
Connecting every standard cell to dual external supply rails so that individual gates can switch their supply voltage cycle-by-cycle.
Inserting High-Vt (HVT) cells along setup-critical paths to maximize drive strength, while deploying Low-Vt (LVT) cells on non-critical paths to limit dynamic power.

Utilizing Low-Vt (LVT) cells along timing-critical paths to meet clock frequency targets while swapping non-critical path cells with High-Vt (HVT) cells to substantially reduce subthreshold leakage power.
